title: Applied ML Eval Harness Standards and Integrated Playbook
author: Sofia Ramirez
summary: Standards and playbook for Redwood's applied ML evaluation harness, covering prompt-set construction, onboarding steps for new models, quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and regression triage procedures.
body:
Overview

This document defines the standard practices and operational playbooks for Redwood's Applied ML evaluation stack (the Eval Harness). It consolidates guidance for: (1) designing and maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks; (2) model onboarding requirements and gating; (3) quality guardrails and monitoring; (4) quantization profile testing and acceptance; and (5) regression triage and remediation workflows. The goal is to ensure consistent, reproducible, and auditable evaluations that protect production quality while enabling efficient model iteration.

Scope

- Eval harness components covered: local test runners, orchestrated CI jobs, annotation UI, metric dashboards, baseline storage, and alerting hooks.
- Workflows: onboarding new model families, performing release regressions, validating quantized variants, and handling production regressions tied to evals.
- Exclusions: research-only probes and exploratory experiments (these belong in Research Drive).

Ownership and Contacts

- Primary owner: Applied ML & Evals team (eng-applied-ml).
- Operational contact: Sofia Ramirez (lead, applied ML).
- SRE integration: eng-sre oncall (pager duty for infra).
- Review cadence: quarterly (performance and coverage review).

Standards and Definitions

- Gold prompt set: small, high-signal set used for gating (typically 50–200 examples).
- Silver prompt set: larger benchmark for performance tracking (500–5,000 examples).
- Baseline: the model/version tagged as production baseline for a workload; all new variants are compared to it.
- Regresion threshold: default statistical significance and absolute delta thresholds used to trigger triage (see Metrics & Thresholds).

Prompt Sets and Benchmarking Guidance

1) Prompt-set design principles:
   - Representativeness: include common user intents and rarer failure modes.
   - Diversity: multiple phrasings, temperatures, and context lengths to cover distributional variance.
   - Deterministic labels: where possible, use tasks with clearly verifiable ground truth to avoid annotation drift.
   - Metadata: every example must include intent, scenario tags, input length bucket, and expected output schema.

2) Dataset hygiene and maintenance:
   - Provenance: record source, author, and last annotation pass date.
   - Versioning: store prompt sets in Git LFS or dataset storage with a semver-like tag: v_MAJOR.MINOR.patch.
   - Ownership: assign a dataset steward responsible for quarterly audits.

3) Benchmarking pipeline:
   - Smoke run: local runner against gold set for quick checks.
   - CI run: scheduled nightly against silver sets, generating detailed metrics and per-example diffs.
   - Canary run: small production traffic split (0.5–2%) for new models under distributor policy.

Model Onboarding Requirements

Prerequisites (must pass before model is eligible for canary):
- Model artifact stored in model registry with manifest (architecture, tokenizer, weights, quantization support).
- Baseline eval: run against gold and silver prompt sets with results uploaded to eval-metrics store.
- Latency and memory profile: 50th/95th/99th percentile on representative hardware (tooling: perf-suite).
- Compatibility tests: tokenizer sanity checks, deterministic sampling seeds, and function-calling end-to-end tests where applicable.

Onboarding checklist (ordered):
1. Create model entry in the registry and attach manifest.
2. Run automated eval harness: gold + silver sets.
3. Review eval report with Applied ML owner (required sign-off).
4. Run quantized builds (see Quantization section) and verify quality delta <= regression threshold.
5. Deploy to canary with feature flag and rollback policy.
6. Monitor metrics for 48–72 hours and validate no production regressions.

Quality Guardrails and Metrics

Primary metrics (collected per-route and per-model):
- Accuracy / pass-rate (task dependent)
- Rouge/BLEU/F1 where applicable
- Hallucination rate (annotated or heuristic-based)
- Truthfulness score (for knowledge tasks)
- Latency P50/P95/P99 and tail behaviour
- Cost per 1k tokens (estimates from token accounting)

Default thresholds (example):
- Regression alert if accuracy drops by >2% absolute vs baseline on gold set.
- Latency SLO breach if P95 increases by >30% vs baseline or crosses 800ms for interactive routes.
- Hallucination increase >1.5x triggers triage.

Monitoring & Alerts:
- Nightly evals post results to dashboards (path: dashboards/evals).
- Alert rules: eval-regression-critical (blocks rollout), eval-regression-warning (notifies owners).

Quantization Profiles and Validation

Purpose: define and validate quantization profiles that trade off memory/throughput vs quality.

Profile types:
- fp16 (baseline on GPU).
- int8-ptq (post-training static quant).
- int4-qat (quant aware training recommended for aggressive compression).

Validation steps for each profile:
1. Functional smoke: tokenization + end-to-end generation sanity checks.
2. Gold eval: run gold prompt set and compare to baseline; record absolute delta per metric.
3. Silver eval: run full silver benchmark for statistically robust comparison.
4. Performance profiling: measure throughput, memory, and cost-per-token.
5. Regression gating: if any key metric exceeds preset regression thresholds, profile must be rejected or retrained.

Recommended acceptance criteria (defaults):
- Max accuracy delta <= 1.5% absolute on gold set for int8-ptq.
- Hallucination delta <= 0.5% absolute.
- Throughput improvement >= 1.8x or memory reduction >= 40% to justify any small quality loss.

Regression Triage Playbook

Triggering events:
- CI nightly eval reports a statistically significant regression vs baseline.
- Canary/prod monitoring alerts flag a drop on live traffic correlated with evals.

High-level triage flow:
1. Triage kickoff: Applied ML lead opens a triage issue and assigns initial owner. Include links to failing examples and eval diffs.
2. Classify the regression: quality, performance, or infra-related.
3. Collect evidence: per-example diffs, deterministic replay scripts, system perf metrics, and recent change list (models, tokenizers, infra).
4. Reproduce: run deterministic local repro; if non-deterministic, run cohort sampling to estimate failure rate.
5. Mitigation: short-term rollback to baseline or reroute traffic; long-term fix scoped with owners and timeline.
6. Postmortem: within 5 business days, publish incident summary, root cause, and remediation plan.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Applied ML owner: lead triage and coordinate fixes.
- Model owner (author): provide fixes and suggested model patches.
- SRE: validate infra changes and perf regressions.
- Product/PM: assess customer impact and communicate externally if needed.

Operational Playbooks and CI Integration

- CI stages should include: lint -> unit tests -> smoke eval (gold) -> silver eval -> artifact publish.
- Nightly regression pipeline: run silver eval suite, update baseline comparisons, and post to dashboards.
- Canary automation: rollback on eval-regression-critical alert or if live-metric breach persists for >1 hour.

Example CLI commands

- Run local gold eval: eval-harness run --set gold --model MODEL_REF --out results.json
- Compare vs baseline: eval-harness compare --baseline BASELINE_REF --candidate results.json --report diff.html
- Generate quant profile: quant-tool profile --model MODEL_REF --type int8-ptq --out profile.json

Documentation and Reporting

- Every model onboarding must include a one-page eval summary in the registry with: key metrics, gold example failures, quant profiles tested, and canary results.
- Quarterly eval health report: coverage, top regressions, and dataset drift indicators.

Appendices

A. Example Git LFS layout for prompt sets:
   datasets/prompt-sets/<workload>/<version>/<gold|silver>.jsonl

B. Standard metric schema (CSV or JSONL columns): example_id, input_text, expected_output, candidate_output, pass_bool, metric_vals, tags

C. Escalation contacts:
   - Applied ML Pager: eng-applied-ml-pager (primary)
   - SRE Pager: eng-sre-pager (secondary)
